title: Composite DR runbook: staged promotion, KV drift detection, and adaptive circuit-breaker calibration
creator: Sofia Martínez
description: Consolidated runbook for active-passive cutovers that focuses on staged promotion, continuous KV drift detection, and adaptive circuit-breaker calibration to protect SLOs during failovers. This ticket delivers: 1) an operator-facing step-by-step runbook for live drills and emergency switchover; 2) automated verification checks for backups and restores including hash-based snapshot compare and sample query replay; 3) a short feedback loop for circuit-breaker threshold tuning tied to observed token latency/cost signals; 4) a rehearsal play schedule and post-drill audit template.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runbook exercised in a full dry-run (no traffic) with snapshot-compare verification; 2) One scheduled live drill with canary traffic demonstrating <15% SLO regression and successful automatic shedding; 3) KV drift detector produces consistent diff metrics and alerts on >0.1% key divergence; 4) Post-drill runbook edits merged and runbook approved in console-ops docs; 5) Security review completed and signoff recorded.
runbook_steps: Preconditions: inform on-call rotation, freeze non-emergency deploys for maintenance window, ensure latest snapshots exist in encrypted archive and cross-region storage.
Step 1 — Prepare target passive region: verify node pool health, GPU availability, and model artifact integrity (checksums).
Step 2 — Lock write paths to primary: enable soft-fence that redirects new writes to a staging queue; keep read traffic mirrored.
Step 3 — Snapshot and export: take KV snapshot, compute rolling Merkle-style checksums for segments, push to passive region storage; capture tokenstore and ephemeral caches snapshot.
Step 4 — Incremental restore: stream snapshot to passive region, apply incremental logs, and run replica reconciliation with sampling window.
Step 5 — KV drift detection: run sample of 10k keys withS deterministic queries, compute divergence ratio, and flag >0.1% for manual review.
Step 6 — Promote passive to warm-primary (staged): enable read-only serving, attach a read-only route in the console and run labeled canary traffic (1-5% by latency tier).
Step 7 — Adaptive circuit-breaker calibration: start with conservative thresholds (latency x1.5, error-rate 2x baseline) and auto-relax based on 30m moving window of P99 and error rate.
Step 8 — Progressive ramp: if canaries pass, increase traffic in 5 stages with 10–20 minute observation windows; if thresholds breach, trigger automatic rollback stage and increase shedding.
Step 9 — Full cutover: once >90% of traffic validated and KV drift <0.01% for 30m, flip production routes and demote old primary to standby mode with read-only access for verification.
Step 10 — Post-cutover verification: run end-to-end samples, synthetic prompts, billing/cost sanity checks, and trace comparisons for request paths.
Step 11 — Restore write-paths carefully: re-enable writes to new primary and monitor consumer lag on ingestion queues.
Step 12 — Cleanup and snapshot: take full post-cutover backup and record checksums; annotate runbook with observed timings and anomalies.
Step 13 — Postmortem and runbook update: within 48 hours, capture lessons learned, concrete improvements, and ETA for follow-up fixes.
Step 14 — Reconcile secrets and KMS rotation tasks if passive environment used alternate keys; coordinate with security team before returning to normal ops.
rollback_plan: If any stage breaches SLO thresholds for >5 minutes or KV divergence exceeds defined limits, trigger the automated rollback motion: 1) traffic fencing—immediately reattach routed traffic back to primary; 2) enable circuit-breaker strict mode to shed noncritical requests and preserve control-plane ops; 3) run snapshot-integrity compare and, if necessary, rehydrate a fresh passive from last known-good snapshot; 4) escalate to DR lead and open incident document. All rollback start/end timestamps must be recorded.
validation_tests: Backup integrity: checksum validation for 100% of artifact bundles and spot-check 1000 random keys post-upload.
Restore fidelity: end-to-end replay of 200 synthetic requests per model profile with output hash comparison against golden responses.
KV drift sensitivity: injection test that deliberately flips 0.05% of keys to confirm detector triggers only above threshold.
Circuit-breaker behaviour: simulated latency spike test to validate breaker trips at configured thresholds and auto-relax behavior after 30m of stability.
Load-shedding policy: low-priority traffic drop simulation to verify graceful degradation without control-plane failures.
drill_schedule: Dry-run #1 (no traffic): 2026-03-05, participants: SRE, Infra, Runtime, PM; objective: baseline timings and restore validation.
Canary live drill: 2026-03-18, participants: SRE, Runtime, Customer Success; objective: 5% canary traffic, validate shedding and SLO impact.
Full dry-run with staged ramp: 2026-04-02, participants: cross-functional; objective: end-to-end rehearsal with progressive promotion.
notes_and_assumptions: Assumes passive region has compatible GPU SKU family and that model artifacts support resumed KV cache warmup. Assumes network egress quotas are sufficient for snapshot transfer. Post-cutover cost spike expected; finance notified.
post_dr_actions: Capture granular latency/cost deltas per token and publish to cost-slo dashboard.
Adjust circuit-breaker parameters based on observed false-positive trips and set new defaults in runtime-config.
Schedule a follow-up engineering spike to speed up incremental restores if restore window exceeded target.
File any config drift as follow-up tickets and track in this project.
